title: Outbound licensing and machine-readable reuse terms for endia.de's own explainer pages
question: Under which outbound licence and machine-readable terms should endia.de publish its own explainer pages so that sibling KUEPER projects and the public may reuse them, given that a page may combine original text, quotations from the novels (publisher and author rights) and adapted third-party material under its own licence? What do the Creative Commons 4.0 licences, the § 44b UrhG / Art. 4 Directive (EU) 2019/790 text-and-data-mining reservation, CC REL and schema.org licence markup actually permit or require; how must a mixed-rights page be attributed and partitioned so that an open licence does not purport to license material the platform does not own; and what does that imply for the ecosystem's 'link instead of copy' norm?
why_now: README.md line 15 sets 'link instead of copy' as the binding ecosystem norm but names no licence, and lines 19-23 make this repository a node that other projects address through external tasks. RES-20261022-5C288045 analysed only inbound reuse of other providers' material. The licence and rights carve-up gate whether explainer pages can be reused across KUEPER at all, and are cheapest to fix before any content exists.
real_world_anchor: The Creative Commons 4.0 licence suite, § 44b UrhG and Art. 4 of Directive (EU) 2019/790 (text-and-data-mining reservation), CC REL and schema.org licence markup.
novelty_reason: RES-20261022-5C288045 asks which licences and statutory rules permit endia.de to reference, quote, embed or adapt other providers' digital-literacy material — an inbound question about what the platform may take. This is the inverse: which licence the platform grants for its own pages, how a mixed-rights page (novel quotations, third-party material and original text) constrains that grant, and whether a TDM reservation should be asserted. No prior topic addresses outbound licensing, rights partitioning or TDM reservation.
